tool_summary: Removes empty directories. Fails on non-empty directories, which makes it considerably lower risk than rm -r.
platform_notes: Behavior is consistent between GNU and BSD rmdir.

rules.description: The -p/--parents flag removes a directory and then attempts to remove each parent directory in the path if it becomes empty, which can remove more of a directory tree than the single named target.
rules.reversible_note: Only removes directories that are empty at the time; will not delete non-empty directories or files, so unintended data loss is unlikely.

rules.description: Removes an empty directory. Fails with an error if the directory is not empty, which limits the blast radius considerably compared to rm -r.
